objects: population-specific PRS; independent target-population validation data
assumptions: Combining multiple population-specific PRS under current practice
conclusion: Combining population-specific PRS ordinarily needs independent target-population genotype and phenotype data that can be nearly impossible to obtain.
scope: Motivation for summary-statistic PRS combination; no impossibility theorem.
span: Finally, in order to combine multiple population-specific PRS, the current practice requires additional data from the target (non-European) population. This includes individual-level genotype and phenotype samples that are independent of the GWAS used to train single-population PRS. In practice, this type of data can be nearly impossible to obtain34.

assumptions: GWAS summary statistics and LD reference panel; full Bayesian default
conclusion: X-Wing fits the PRS model with block Gibbs sampling, recommending 1000 K iterations with 500 K burn-in and default Bayesian fitting without validation tuning.
scope: Recommended iteration counts are settings; no MCMC convergence rate or finite-iteration accuracy guarantee is stated.
span: We employ a simple and efficient block Gibbs sampler to fit the PRS model using GWAS summary statistics and LD reference panel (Supplementary Methods)70. Following Ruan et al.16, we recommend using 1000 × K Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) iterations with the first 500 × K iterations as burn-in. We use the full Bayesian approach as default, which does not require validation data to tune the model.

span: Typically, repeated learning (or cross-validation) requires individual-level genotype and phenotype data since it involves sample splitting. objects: input GWAS; matched LD panels; admixed and multi-ancestry populations
assumptions: Applying X-Wing without individual-level phenotype/genotype validation data
conclusion: Matching LD reference panels to the input GWAS remains crucial, and optimal reference selection for multi-ancestry GWAS and admixed populations is unresolved.
scope: The authors report this limitation despite observed predictive improvements.
span: First, although our method does not require any individual-level sample with both genotype and phenotype information, it remains crucial to have LD reference panels that match the input GWAS. We observed an improvement in PRS performance when applying our method to highly diverse samples such as the PAGE study, but it remains unclear how to best select LD references for multi-ancestry GWAS and admixed populations68.
